KS is a rare disease with an autosomal recessiveness characterized by a triad consisting of bronchiectasia, sinusitis, situs inversus and IgA nephropathies.
KS is an uncommon cause of IgA nephropathies.
Kartagener syndrome, a subgroup of primary cilinary dyskinesia, is a rare cause of immunoglobulin A (IgA) nephropathy.

the clinical features of a patient who was diagnosed with both KS and IgA nephropathic nephritis.
the clinical characteristics of a case of KS complicated by biopsy-proven IgA nephropath.
the clinical features of a case of Kartagener syndrome with complications of immunoglobulin (A) nephropathy, which is a very uncommon disease.

the association of KS/PCD with IgA nephropathies is not a casual event.
KS and/or P CD are not associated with IgA nephropathies, but that they might be associated with other types of nephropathies.

the presence of KS and/or a PCD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of IgA nephropathies, and further research is needed to determine the relationship between these diseases.
